title: CISA BOD 26-04 replaces the fixed KEV clock with risk-based remediation deadlines
summary: CISA's Binding Operational Directive 26-04, 'Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk', consolidates and supersedes the older BOD 19-02 (remediating critical/high internet-facing vulnerabilities) and BOD 22-01 (the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities programme). It moves federal civilian agencies from a single fixed KEV due-date toward remediation windows driven by each asset's internet exposure and risk, and it is paired with CISA forensic-triage implementation guidance. Recent KEV entries already cite BOD 26-04 in their required-action text.
why: The directive only binds US federal civilian agencies, but it is the clearest signal yet of how CISA expects everyone to prioritise patching: by exposure and exploitability rather than CVSS alone. If you run a KEV-aligned SLA, your internal policy language and tooling assumptions (fixed 14/21-day clocks, 'critical first') need to match the new exposure-weighted model, and the forensic-triage guidance raises the bar on what 'remediated' means for an internet-facing asset.
todo: Re-read your vulnerability-management policy against BOD 26-04's risk/exposure model; update any text that still references BOD 19-02 or BOD 22-01.
Make sure your asset inventory records internet exposure per asset, because that now drives the deadline, not just the severity.
Keep KEV ingestion automated (the `known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json` feed) and map each KEV item to exposure before assigning an internal due date.
Add CISA's forensic-triage expectations to your incident runbooks for exploited, internet-facing systems.
effective_note: BOD 26-04 supersedes and revokes BOD 19-02 and BOD 22-01 (CISA Cybersecurity Directives page, checked 2026-11-04).
